open_points.subject: Mapped-node output disclosure class on empty input (A07 vs A13)
open_points.text: A07 rule 3: "No function, edge or flow construct lowers a class." A13 rule 6: mapped outputs are "the highest class among its elements (A07), `open` when empty".
open_points.question: If a mapped node has non-mapped `personal_data` inputs but maps over an empty list, what class must its empty-list outputs carry?
options: Always `open` when the mapped list is empty (literal A13)
Highest class that reached the node, even when no elements ran (A07 monotonic rule)
open_points.default_guess: Always `open` when empty, because A13 states it explicitly.

open_points.subject: Approval requests when request shape changes while one is still `requested`
open_points.text: A10 rule 1: any request difference means prior approval "is no authority" and kernel proceeds "by asking anew". A10 rule 2: records one approval request, "none when a `requested` one for it already exists".
open_points.question: When a pending `requested` approval becomes stale (new request digest), does the kernel replace it with a new `requested` approval or keep waiting on the old one?
options: Keep existing `requested` approval until owner decides it
Mark old request stale/void and create a new `requested` approval immediately
open_points.default_guess: Keep existing `requested` approval until it is decided.

open_points.subject: Choosing an approval when multiple approved-unused approvals match
open_points.text: A10 rule 1 requires "an approved, unused EffectApproval ... whose `request_digest` equals" but does not define selection if more than one exists for the same run/node/element.
open_points.question: If multiple approved-unused approvals match the same send, which one is consumed and recorded as authority?
options: Refuse as ambiguous and require a fresh single approval

open_points.subject: `request_digest` header set boundary
open_points.text: A10 rule 7: approval covers "every header the kernel sends".
open_points.question: Does "every header the kernel sends" include transport-library implicit headers (e.g., Host, Content-Length, Connection, User-Agent) or only headers explicitly set by kernel rules?
options: Only headers explicitly defined by kernel logic
All on-wire headers including client-library/generated ones

open_points.subject: Multipart approval digest stability
open_points.text: A10 rule 7 includes header values in the covered request; for multipart bodies it excludes boundary from body description only: "so the boundary is not part of it."
open_points.question: Is multipart `Content-Type` boundary parameter part of approval matching (via headers), and if not, how is it normalized?
options: Boundary is included via header value (approval may invalidate if boundary changes)
Boundary is normalized/removed for digest comparison
Boundary generation is fixed deterministically so values always match
open_points.default_guess: Boundary is normalized/removed from matching intent.

open_points.subject: First-failure determinism inside list-valued validations
open_points.text: Several rules require "every element fits" (e.g., A12 run input validation, A09 request placement checks, A04 trial-case fit) but do not state which failing element/index is reported first.
open_points.question: When multiple elements in one list input are invalid, what exact element-order rule determines the reported failure?
options: First failing element by list index
open_points.default_guess: First failing element by list index.

open_points.subject: Result semantics of `approve` when approval decision succeeds but send cannot proceed
open_points.text: A10 rule 3: "The approval itself always succeeds; when a pre-send check then fails ... nothing is sent ... approval stays `approved` and unused."
open_points.question: What does the approve operation return in that case: success for the decision only, or refusal/failure because no send happened?
options: Return success for approval decision plus updated run state showing node failure/wait
Return refusal/failure for approve call because send did not occur
open_points.default_guess: Return success for the decision and include resulting run state.
